findings.title: Over-window recommendation omits required structured provenance
findings.what: The detector derives peak-context evidence and states that sessions exceeded 200K tokens where context is evicted and re-sent at cost, but the returned recommendation has no provenance tying those claims to tokenData/computeContextGrowth fields or documenting the threshold inference.
findings.fix: Add a provenance object with observations for the source session count and peakContext field, plus an inference identifying OVER_WINDOW and qualifying the eviction/cost interpretation.
findings.acceptance: A firing recommendation passes the repository provenance validator and its observations identify tokenData-derived peakContext values and the applied threshold; add a test asserting this.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the only evidence is a display string at lines 31-33 and the returned object through line 43 contains no provenance; the fix is illustrative, so no validated-snippet defect was claimed.

findings.title: Command identity is mistaken for duplicate output identity
findings.what: callFingerprint groups by tool name and command/preview only. Repeated executions of the same command can return different content and different sizes, yet the group is labeled a duplicate result and reclaim is calculated as (count-1) times the maximum result size. This can overstate both deterministically reclaimable tokens and estimated savings.
findings.fix: Require a stable result-content digest before classifying outputs as duplicates, or rename/recalculate this bucket as repeated-command output using the measured size of each repeat and explicitly qualify it as an estimate.
findings.acceptance: Add a case with the same command returning different result digests/sizes; it must not be reported as duplicate output. Identical digests must still produce reclaim equal to the actual repeated payload sizes and valid provenance.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed the fingerprint contains no result identity and lines 191-204 use the maximum observed byte count for every repeat. The dispatched tests cover repeated commands with equal fixture sizes but no differing-result adversarial case.

findings.title: Paste deduplication retains full normalized copies of every pasted block
findings.what: pasteKey allocates a whitespace-normalized copy of each complete pasted block, and pasteAgg retains that full string both as its Map key and as sample data. Large or mostly unique pasted content therefore adds substantial allocation and retained-memory pressure on top of the already-loaded session corpus.
findings.fix: Use a streaming/stable content digest plus length as the aggregation key and retain only the bounded 40-character preview needed for evidence; resolve rare hash collisions with a secondary bounded check if necessary.
findings.acceptance: A memory/latency probe over many large unique pasted blocks demonstrates bounded retained key/sample data rather than retention of every normalized block, while duplicate detection and displayed previews remain reproducible.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the complete normalized string is created at line 103, used as the Map key at line 250, and retained again as sample at line 253; only a 40-character preview is ultimately consumed.

findings.title: Repeated-compactions recommendation lacks claim provenance
findings.what: The detector reports observed compaction counts and asserts that each compacted summary re-bills tokens on every subsequent turn, but the recommendation contains no structured observations or inference identifying the source artifacts and fields.
findings.fix: Emit provenance observations for computeCompactionRisk compactionsObserved/session identifiers and an inference that separately qualifies the recurring-token-cost claim.
findings.acceptance: A firing recommendation passes provenance validation, cites the compaction-risk source field, and a test asserts the structured observations and inference.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed the result object from lines 29-50 contains evidence strings but no provenance, and the dispatched test verifies only firing and suppression.

findings.title: Repo-map context-waste claims are emitted without structured provenance
findings.what: The recommendation claims files are stable/read-only, structurally important, re-read across sessions, and responsible for a precise aggregate token cost, but returns no provenance connecting those claims to repoMap file fields, reread measurements, imports, churn, or parseFileReread.
findings.fix: Add structured observations for candidate paths, churn, exported/config/centrality signals, reread sessions/token waste, and any reclaim scope calculation; distinguish measured fields from the inference that pinning removes the repeated cost.
findings.acceptance: Representative stable-API, config-backed, and centrality recommendations pass provenance validation and tests assert the cited repoMap/parseFileReread fields and computed aggregate values.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed candidates and totals originate at lines 136-178 and reclaim fields at lines 180-238, while the returned recommendation at lines 252-273 has evidence and reclaim metadata but no provenance object.
